summary.going_well: The agent recognized a fixed-payment home equity loan and explained its collateral risk <ref job="SRJ_oMN34EtZueat" item="item_ee276e84-a3b">before continuing discovery</ref>. It distinguished a cash-out refinance from borrowing against the existing mortgage <ref job="SRJ_7zsZk4dMPWA8" item="item_a92747ef-e84">with a keep-or-replace question</ref>. It offered borrowers a choice of soft review or summary <ref job="SRJ_jmob6ZzFYqtZ" item="item_fa216b02-0dd">without selecting for them</ref>.
summary.to_improve: Complete the HELOC variable-rate comfort check before offering next steps. Remove blanket conventional-refinance claims, and handle declined employer names without losing track of remaining questions. Keep acknowledgments neutral rather than endorsing borrowers’ numbers or plans.

issues.description: In the HELOC conversation, the agent disclosed variable-rate risk but asked only whether the overall structure made sense <ref job="SRJ_yXMxdMBrDvRF" item="item_181e809c-2cc">rather than whether the borrower was comfortable with a variable rate</ref>; it then <ref job="SRJ_yXMxdMBrDvRF" item="item_ee3ddb43-32c">offered the final choice</ref> without collecting that answer.
issues.suggestion: Add a distinct variable-rate comfort question to the HELOC discovery checklist, and block the final offer until it has been answered.
issues.label: Discovery gap

issues.description: In two refinance conversations, the agent presented conventional loans as having <ref job="SRJ_A9eVysc8eVqB" item="item_46915727-e67">“no upfront government fees,” no permanent mortgage insurance at 20% equity, and “higher loan limits”</ref>, repeating those <ref job="SRJ_7zsZk4dMPWA8" item="item_34134979-ff9">unqualified advantages</ref> without establishing which alternatives or terms applied.
issues.suggestion: Replace the blanket comparison with conditional, verified product language; defer fee, insurance-removal, and loan-limit specifics to the eligibility review or licensed officer.
issues.label: Product accuracy

issues.description: When borrowers declined to give an employer name, the agent went straight to the final offer <ref job="SRJ_yXMxdMBrDvRF" item="item_0cef2c1b-4c4">after one refusal</ref> <ref job="SRJ_yXMxdMBrDvRF" item="item_ee3ddb43-32c">in the HELOC flow</ref> and likewise <ref job="SRJ_A9eVysc8eVqB" item="item_a0f5f94d-d55">after another refusal</ref> <ref job="SRJ_A9eVysc8eVqB" item="item_1e1b2f90-26a">in the refinance flow</ref>. It neither acknowledged the boundary nor checked for other outstanding discovery questions.
issues.suggestion: Treat a declined employer name as an explicit refusal rather than a completed flow: acknowledge it, retain the supplied employment type and tenure, and ask any other outstanding questions before the final offer.
issues.label: Flow control

issues.description: The agent repeatedly evaluated borrower-provided numbers or plans before any review, calling a credit score <ref job="SRJ_7zsZk4dMPWA8" item="item_a4db63e8-4d8">“great”</ref> and a roof project <ref job="SRJ_oMN34EtZueat" item="item_38c620f1-3b0">“a great use of equity”</ref>.
issues.suggestion: Use neutral acknowledgments for self-reported credit, finances, timelines, and plans; reserve assessments for the review or licensed loan officer.
